examples: The weather is really nice today.
Because it was cold I wore many clothes.
How is the weather on the weekend?
nuance: 날씨 covers general weather conditions and is one of the most common small-talk topics in Korea.
mistakes: Saying 날씨는 좋아요 by default when neutral 날씨가 좋아요 is more natural

examples: Because it rained I brought an umbrella.
nuance: With 비 Koreans say 비가 와요 (rain comes) rather than a direct verb for to rain, so the verb 오다 is essential.
mistakes: Saying 비가 해요 instead of the correct 비가 와요

examples: It snows a lot in winter.
It is snowing and the wind blows too.
It is snowing outside so the road is white.
nuance: 눈 also means eye, so the same spelling has two meanings and context tells them apart; like rain it uses 눈이 와요.
mistakes: Confusing 눈 snow with 눈 eye without checking the context

examples: The wind blows a lot today.
It is cold because the wind blows.
In spring a warm wind blows.
nuance: 바람 pairs with the verb 불다 (to blow), not 오다, so saying 바람이 불어요 is the natural way to describe wind.
mistakes: Saying 바람이 와요 instead of the correct 바람이 불어요

usage: there are clouds in the sky
examples: The sky is really clear today.
There are many clouds in the sky.
The rain stopped and the sky turned blue.
nuance: 하늘 means the physical sky and often appears with location particle 에 when something is in it, as in 하늘에 구름이 있어요.
mistakes: Using 에서 instead of 에 for static location in the sky

usage: there are clouds in the sky
examples: There is not a single cloud in the sky.
It is cloudy because clouds gathered.
nuance: 구름 is counted and described with 많다 or 끼다 rather than 오다, and it commonly sits in the sky with the particle 에.
mistakes: Saying 구름이 와요 by mistake the way one says 비가 와요

nuance: 색 means color and the longer form 색깔 means the same thing in casual speech; both attach color names like 빨간색 and 파란색.
mistakes: Forgetting the object particle in 색을 좋아해요

nuance: 빨간색 is the noun for red while the modifier 빨간 goes directly before a noun, as in 빨간 사과 for a red apple.
mistakes: Saying 빨간색 사과 when natural speech uses 빨간 사과

nuance: 파란색 is the noun for blue and the modifier form 파란 attaches before a noun, as in 파란 하늘 for a blue sky.
mistakes: Mixing up 파란색 blue and 초록색 green for natural objects

examples: In spring many yellow flowers bloom.
nuance: 노란색 is the noun for yellow and the modifier 노란 goes before a noun, as in 노란 꽃 for a yellow flower.
mistakes: Writing 노란 as 노랑 when modifying a noun directly

examples: It snowed in winter so the world is white.
The white snow is really pretty.
nuance: 하얀색 is the noun for white and the modifier 하얀 goes before a noun, as in 하얀 눈 for white snow; 흰색 is also common.
mistakes: Confusing 하얀색 white with 회색 gray

examples: I want to buy a black car.
nuance: 검은색 is the noun for black and the modifier 검은 goes before a noun, as in 검은 옷 for black clothes; 까만색 is a common variant.
mistakes: Saying 검은색 옷 stiffly when 검은 옷 is more natural
